title.rendered: In Everything Give Thanks: Thanks in the Middle of It All | The Thankful Heart, Day 2

excerpt.rendered: 1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 calls us to rejoice always, pray without ceasing and in everything give thanks. Day 2 of The Thankful Heart.

content.rendered:
Paul did not say “for everything give thanks.” He said “in everything.” You are not asked to thank God for the trouble. You are invited to thank Him in it, because He is still in it with you.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, November 16, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 2

Today’s Scripture

“Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, in everything give thanks; for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.”
1 Thessalonians 5:16-18 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Yesterday we stood at the gate and entered with thanksgiving. Today Paul shows us how to stay inside. Three short lines, almost like a rhythm for the whole of life: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, in everything give thanks. Not once a week. Not only when the news is good. Always, without ceasing, in everything.

The church in Thessalonica was not a comfortable church. Acts 17 tells us it was born in a riot. Paul had to leave the city by night. The believers he left behind faced pressure from their neighbours and grief over loved ones who had died. Into that setting Paul wrote these words. He was not writing to people with easy lives. He was writing to people who had discovered that joy and thanks do not depend on easy lives.

Look closely at the small word “in.” Paul does not ask us to call evil good or to pretend pain is pleasant. He says “in everything give thanks.” In the hospital corridor in Nairobi. In the traffic in Lagos. In the job search in London. In the waiting room, the empty bank account, the long season. In every one of those places, there is still something to thank God for, because He is there. His presence did not leave when the trouble arrived (Hebrews 13:5).

Then notice where this thanksgiving comes from: “the will of God in Christ Jesus for you.” This is not a law handed down to make us try harder. It is the life of Christ flowing through people who are in Christ. Jesus gave thanks at the table on the night He was betrayed (1 Corinthians 11:23-24). The same thankful Son now lives in you. When you give thanks in a hard place, you are not manufacturing something. You are letting His life speak.

So try this today. When something goes wrong, before you react, add one sentence: “Lord, I thank You that You are with me in this.” You do not have to feel it first. Say it, and let the words remind your heart of what is already true. Thanks spoken in everything slowly turns into joy always.

How the Thankful Heart Lives

It gives thanks in everything, not for everything. God is not the author of the trouble, but He is present in it.

It flows from Christ, not from effort. Thanksgiving is the will of God in Christ Jesus, His life at work in you.

It keeps the conversation open. Rejoicing, praying and thanking become one steady rhythm with the Father.

Declaration

Lord, I thank You that You will never leave me nor forsake me (Hebrews 13:5), so in every situation I face, You are already there. I rejoice always, I keep my heart in conversation with You, and in everything I give thanks, for this is Your will for me in Christ Jesus (1 Thessalonians 5:16-18). I thank You that the life of Your thankful Son lives in me. Whatever this day brings, I will find You in it and thank You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
